Read the agent's drafts, check them, write the report files

Source: R/ai_requests.R
tfl_ai_collect_answers.Rd

The person's check of what the agent wrote (tfl_ai_prepare()): each request's drafts (ai/spec/outputs/<id>.yml, one a report) are read as the request's answer, checked against the request (tfl_ai_check(): the schema, the analyses, the ADaM summary, the study's files) and, when they have no error, written anew as the study's report files – the column widths filled, the assumptions numbered (spec/_assumptions.yml, tfl_ai_assumptions()), the draft's ai: block (its assumptions, what is marked to confirm: tfl_ai_confirm()) kept. A draft with errors is left as it is: its repair prompt (tfl_ai_repair_prompt()) goes to repairs, to paste into the agent's chat; check again when the agent has fixed it. A draft YAML cannot read is refused with why, for the agent to fix its form.

Usage

tfl_ai_collect_answers(
  study_dir,
  requests = file.path("ai", "requests"),
  repairs = file.path("ai", "repairs"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

Arguments

study_dir

The study folder.

requests, repairs

The folders, under study_dir.

overwrite

TRUE (default) to write over report files already there: a draft checked again replaces its report.

Value

A tfl_ai_collected: a list with reports (a data frame, one row a report: request, output_id, status – ok, warning, error, no answer (no draft yet) –, problems (how many), first (the first problem), problems_text (all of them, one a line), file (the report's ai/spec/outputs/<id>.yml when written, else NA), repair (the request's repair prompt, else NA)), next_steps (a request's next step, named by the request), next_kind and next_args (the same step as a kind and its values, for a screen to say in its own words – see The next step's kinds), assumptions (the study's spec/_assumptions.yml for these reports: output_id, where, item, assumption, value, question, id – the assumption's A<n> – and kind – its K<n>, tfl_ai_assumptions()), stray (drafts no request asks for), requests (the requests' folder), templates (each request's setting, tfl_ai_prepare()'s templates: a logical named by the request), manifest and manifest_file (below).

The next step's kinds

next_steps is English text; next_kind names the same step by a word, with its values in next_args, so a screen can say it in its own language. The kinds, and the values each carries (drafts: the request's draft files, comma-separated):

answer

no draft yet: request (the request file), drafts (the files the agent writes).

fix_answer

a draft could not be read (its YAML, or no id): drafts (the files refused).

answer_again

the drafts could not be checked: drafts.

repair

the drafts have errors and a repair prompt was written: repair (the prompt file), drafts.

see_problem

the report files could not be written (the problem is in reports).

warnings

written, with warnings to read.

done

written, nothing to do.

sheet_missing

a sheet's request: written, but missing (the TOC items) have no draft.

add_missing

written, but missing have no draft: drafts (theirs).

none_asked

the drafts are none of the reports asked for: asked, has.

tfl_ai_run() adds three, for a report that passed its checks: not_built (reports, not built in this run: Rscript run.R <request>), no_package (report, package: R has no such package), build_failed (report, problem, repair).

The manifest is every report the drafts make, for the person to check the count against the TOC (one TOC row can be several reports): a data frame, one row a report: request, toc, output_id, title, split, listed (NA: a request not answered or not read, its reports as asked) and status (the report's, as in reports). It is written to ai/manifest.csv (UTF-8) beside the requests' folder, anew at each collection. The paths are relative to study_dir. Its print is a summary: each request's status, its reports and the next step.

See also

tfl_ai_prepare(), tfl_ai_confirm(), tfl_ai_adopt().
